reason: The carrier needs to hold both cores, so placing it on the cold transfer bench seems like a useful first step. It's the only offered action.
expectation: I expect the carrier to be positioned for loading the cores, though I'm unsure whether this also starts its cooling.

effect: The bench chilled the carrier and confirmed that both cradles can hold whole cores with their surrounding ice.
reaction: The room for surrounding ice is reassuring, since it preserves context for the receiving lab.
reason: The conditioned carrier is ready, and loading the stored source core is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the source core to be placed in one chilled cradle, though I don't know whether another transfer step will be needed.

effect: The source core is in the carrier's first compartment, leaving the second ready for the other core.
reaction: The separate compartments make the transfer easy to follow.
reason: Loading the case with the articulated body is the only offered combination and should fill the remaining compartment.
expectation: I expect the band core to move into the carrier while remaining sealed and cold; flight cooling may still require another step.

effect: Both cores are now in separate cradles in the carrier, ready for transfer to flight cooling.
reaction: Seeing the folded outline again makes the specimen feel tangible, and keeping the two sites separate is reassuring.
reason: The lander's refrigerated sample bay is the remaining destination, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the packed carrier to be connected to flight cooling, completing the goal, though the result may reveal another requirement.

effect: The carrier is connected to powered flight cooling, completing the goal of bringing both cores aboard cold.
reaction: The buffer bridging the transfer makes the cooling sequence feel complete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Chilling the carrier was the most worthwhile step because it explained how the whole cores and their surrounding ice could be preserved for the receiving lab.

leastWorthwhile.text: Loading the two cores felt repetitive because each was the only available combination, though the separate compartments were clear.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the carrier's thermal buffer to bridge the transfer before powered flight cooling took over.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each had a clear role in preparing, loading or cooling the samples.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I want to know what the receiving lab finds in the cores, although this chapter's choices were straightforward.
